medSchoolStudLife.leaveOfAbsence: Students who are unable to complete required courses or clerkships due to illness, hardship or special circumstances must immediately contact the Office of Student Affairs.  The Associate Dean for Student Affairs may approve short-term leave or withdrawal for periods of 6 weeks or less.  Leave periods of time greater than six weeks requires review and approval of the Medical Student Promotion and Performance Committee (MSPPC).
medSchoolStudLife.organizationActivities: VTCSOM encourages students to form VTC Student Clubs, to initiate or become involved with specialty interest groups, and to become involved with regional and national professional medical and specialty organizations.  The Medical Student Government, in collaboration with the Office of Student Affairs, coordinates these activities.
medSchoolStudLife.setting: The Virginia Tech Carilion School of Medicine is located on the Virginia Tech Health Sciences and Technology campus, along with the Fralin Biomedical Research Institute and adjacent to Carilion Roanoke Memorial Hospital (CRMH) in Roanoke, VA. The purpose-built medical school building is a dedicated learning environment that has been designed around the patient-centered curriculum. Roanoke offers a diverse mix of outdoor, cultural, historical and entertainment activities.
medSchoolStudLife.housing: A range of affordable housing options exist within a short drive, trolley or bicycle ride. Prices typically range from $1000/month for a 1B/1B to $1,500/month for a 2B/2B.
medSchoolStudLife.supportSystems: LGBTQ+ Resource Center provides support to all Virginia Tech and VTC students: https://ccc.vt.edu/pride_center.html
medSchoolStudLife.supportSystemsForDisabilities: VTCSOM is committed to providing all accepted and current students with opportunities to take full advantage of our educational, academic, and community programs. We recognize that students with documented disabilities may need accommodations to fully participate and encourage students to disclose with VT’s Services to Students with Disabilities (SSD) and contact SSD for accommodations support as early as possible. https://medicine.vtc.vt.edu/student-life/academic-services/disability-advocacy-support.html
medSchoolStudLife.wellnessPrograms: VTC offers a robust student wellness program. Check out our webpage for more details: https://medicine.vtc.vt.edu/student-life/student-wellness.html
medSchoolStudLife.campusCulture: Nestled in the city of Roanoke, VTC combines the serenity of the Blue Ridge Mountains with a dynamic community that celebrates diversity, collaboration, and growth. Here, students bring unique experiences and perspectives, fostering a learning environment that values excellence. With Virginia Tech's motto "Ut Prosim" in mind, students learn from their patients, peers, and the world around them while committing to lifelong growth in knowledge, compassion, and competence. Beyond academics, we pride ourselves on being a close-knit community that supports one another while also we balancing this unique bond with a strong commitment to professionalism and achievement. Blending academic rigor with the vibrant arts, outdoor recreation, and the welcoming spirit of Roanoke, life at VTC offers a unique balance of hard work, heartfelt connection, and an unwavering commitment to making a difference.

medSchoolCurriculum.patientInteraction: Begins the first month of Year 1
medSchoolCurriculum.clinicalRotations: Clinical rotations begin in second year
medSchoolCurriculum.curricularHighlights: Small teams work in a problem-based learning format using patient cases. Ample time is dedicated to providing students with the opportunity to learn and practice clinical skills using lectures, panel discussions, movies, workshops, simulation models, standardized and real patients. Over the four year curriculum, each VTC student must complete a hypothesis-driven research project guided by a mentoring team, provide a written document suitable for publication, and present their work in an appropriate venue. The VTC Health Systems Science and Interprofessionalism Practice curriculum fosters collaboration among VTC students and healthcare teams to develop the foundational knowledge and skills necessary for practice in diverse healthcare settings.
medSchoolCurriculum.primaryCarePrograms: All students participate in the LACE (Longitudinal Ambulatory Care Experience) Program during their first two years of school.  During the Phase II, there is a required 6 week Family Medicine Clerkship, as well as opportunities for experience in Primary Care Pediatrics, Internal Medicine, OB/GYN clerkships and rural medicine electives.  Interested students are encouraged to participate in primary care research projects as well as take clinical electives in areas of interest during their 3rd and 4th years of school.
medSchoolCurriculum.researchPrograms: Virginia Tech Carilion School of Medicine students have the opportunity to conduct research projects under the mentorship of faculty research team leaders at the Fralin Biomedical Research Institute at VTC, which is located in a state-of-the-art research building connected to the medical school. The Fralin Biomedical Research Institute opened in 2010 with the goal of building innovative, interdisciplinary research programs for preventing, diagnosing, treating, and curing disease and enhancing healthy lives. The institute has since built nationally recognized research programs in cognitive and computational neuroscience, brain development and disease, addiction/substance abuse, brain cancer, cardiovascular sciences, wound healing, health behavior and human development, and immunology. Research Institute faculty members serve as principal investigators on research grants with an annual value of $18M and have annual research expenditures of over $25 million.
medSchoolCurriculum.communityServiceText: Students participate in various student-run, physician-supervised free clinics and other community service opportunities
medSchoolCurriculum.researchThesisText: A research manuscript of publishable quality
medSchoolCurriculum.affiliatedHospitals: Carilion operates 7 not-for-profit hospitals and 220 outpatient clinics, serving ~1.7 million residents and is the only level 1 Trauma Center and Pediatric Trauma Center in western VA.
medSchoolCurriculum.gradingSystem:

Required clinical rotations are graded

medSchoolInformation.generalInformation: Virginia Tech Carilion School of Medicine is a public, four-year medical school offering the doctor of medicine (M.D.) degree as the ninth college of Virginia Tech with clinical training through Carilion Clinic. Our mission is to matriculate academically capable students who demonstrate passion for medicine, research, and community. Using an innovative, patient-centered curriculum, VTCSOM addresses the need for physicians who impact their communities and improve health systems. The curriculum provides an exemplary education in basic and clinical sciences and skills, but transcends traditional medical education by providing a solid foundation in health systems science, interprofessionalism, and disciplines of research. We envision that VTCSOM students will be highly sought after by residency programs and will become physician thought leaders in their chosen fields of medicine.
medSchoolInformation.missionStatement: VTC's mission is to develop physician thought leaders through inquiry, research and discovery, using an innovative curriculum based on adult learning methods in a patient-centered context. Our graduates will be physicians with outstanding clinical skills and significantly enhanced research capabilities who will remain life-long learners. The VTC physician will have an understanding of the importance of interprofessionalism to enable them to thrive in a modern healthcare team.

medSchoolApplication.amcasLettersText: Reference letters should reflect the breadth of your academic, medical, and volunteer experiences. We accept letters of recommendation, pre-health committee evaluations, and centralized reference letter packages electronically via AMCAS Letters. A committee letter with a pre-health advisor's endorsement, or a total of three to seven letters of recommendation, are a sufficient number of personal recommendations to support your application.
medSchoolApplication.letterGuidance: While we require a minimum of three letters, we strongly recommend you provide letters from your spectrum of experiences, including: a science or math professor (required), research mentor/PI, and a letter from a professional in the medical field.
medSchoolApplication.stateResAfterMatric: A student who is in Virginia primarily to attend college is not considered to be a domiciled resident. There is no separate in-state tuition.
medSchoolApplication.additionalInfo: As the transitions past various public health restrictions continue, online alternatives to traditional coursework, labs, and pass/fail credits will be considered and reviewed on a case-by-case basis. Courses and labs taken via traditional instructional delivery are, of course, accepted routinely.

medSchoolFinancial.financialAid:
The Virginia Tech Carilion School of Medicine offers a competitive financial aid package including private scholarship and loans. The financial status of the applicant is not considered in the admissions process. Students have access to Title IV federal loans (Stafford and Graduate PLUS) through the Free Application for Federal Student Aid (FAFSA), as well as other private/alternative student loan programs. Students are normally eligible to borrow up to the full cost of attendance, if needed. The Office of Financial Aid provides assistance with the financial aid application process, individual budgeting, loan repayment options, and debt management. 

For financial aid information, please email: vtcsomfinaid@vt.edu

medSchoolPrograms.name: Students at VTC can choose to enroll in the MPH program at Virginia Tech in their 3rd year of studies, which requires an additional year for the practicum. Students then return to VTC in their fourth year to begin their clerkship rotations and graduate at the end of their fifth year of studies.

medSchoolTimeline.eventDetail: Accepted applicants have the option to "Plan to Enroll" to Virginia Tech Carilion School of Medicine through AMCAS
Accepted applicants with multiple acceptances must hold only three acceptances and withdraw from all other schools
Accepted students have the option to "Commit to Enroll" to the school or program to which they plan to matriculate
If you receive additional acceptances after April 30, it is your responsibility to promptly notify any school you decide to not attend.

medSchoolAcceptance.waitlistProcedure: Interviewed applicants not initially accepted are re-evaluated in April. Qualified applicants are offered a seat or held on an active wait list until the incoming class matriculates.

medSchoolSelection.oldestPrereqDate: VTC does not have a cut-off for oldest date prerequisite coursework can be completed.
medSchoolSelection.selectionFactors: VTC offers a four-year M.D. degree and admits both Virginia state and out-of-state residents. Applicants must be U.S. citizens or U.S. permanent residents. VTC is committed to attracting learners who will likely achieve academic success in the rigorous academic setting of medical school, while experiencing further growth in other important aspects of professionalism. Our admissions process identifies candidates with evidence of leadership, scholarship, research, service to others, and motivation for a career in medicine as evidenced by superior academic credentials and experiences. VTC seeks individuals whose accomplishments reveal originality and a capacity for independent, critical thinking. Those who are interested in a life-long career of inquiry, including the practice of evidence-based medicine, clinical and basic science research, and scholarship, are encouraged to apply.
medSchoolSelection.preMedShadowText: Continue building your portfolio of working with patients by gaining medically-related experiences, such as physician shadowing, volunteering at a clinic or blood drive, working as an EMT or a medical scribe, or otherwise getting some hands-on medical experience. This will demonstrate your commitment and help you remember why you’re tackling this application process.
